title: Orange juice, 100%, with calcium added, frozen, reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: Orange juice, 100%, with calcium added is a frozen concentrate that, once reconstituted, provides a fully natural juice with enhanced calcium content. The juice is made from ripe oranges and undergoes rapid freezing, preserving vitamin C and other nutrients. Calcium is added in a soluble form that fully dissolves during reconstitution.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing for a few minutes retains over 90% of vitamin C compared with traditional pasteurised juice.
Calcium is added as micro‑crystalline particles that dissolve completely when water is added.
Reconstituted juice tastes and smells like fresh‑pressed juice but can be stored longer without quality loss.
Orange juice is one of the world’s most popular beverages, with more than 70 million tonnes consumed annually.
The drink is often used in sports nutrition because of its vitamin C and calcium combination.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Added calcium strengthens bones and teeth, especially important for children, adolescents and older adults.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The juice contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for cell division and especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Being mostly water, the juice helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural sugars may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the juice can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Vitamin C can affect the efficacy of certain drugs, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, sauces and marinades. To reconstitute the frozen concentrate, add the specified amount of cold water, stir well and chill before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen concentrate at –18 °C or lower. After reconstitution, store in the refrigerator for no more than 3–4 days. Do not leave the juice at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
